prices: Bath entry (not included) – adults / from 16 / from 6
dir.offers: Hourly rental of hard and inflatable boards (over 100 boards at staffed self-service stations), beginner courses for children and adults, private lessons, SUP yoga and a SUP city tour.
dir.ohNote: Usually open daily 09:00-20:00 in good weather; in bad weather the facility may close from 14:00, and stations are not always staffed in changeable weather - call ahead. Subscribers: self-service 07:15-20:00.
dir.req: Swimming ability required. Teens from 14 may rent a board on their own; children under 30 kg can ride on an adult's SUP. Rental includes board, one paddle per person, life vest and dry bag. Bath entry fee not included. Reservations only for groups of 5+.
dir.about: On the Enge side of the lower lake, Supkultur runs its biggest day-rental station inside Strandbad Mythenquai, a short way along the quay from Belvoirpark. Over a hundred boards from Indiana and Fanatic, both hard and inflatable, are handed out from staffed stations, so you can simply turn up, take a board and paddle out along the western shore with the city behind you and the Alps ahead. Children and adults can book beginner courses or private lessons here, and the programme also includes SUP yoga and a guided city tour. It suits first-timers who want staff on hand as much as regulars after an hour on the water. Kayaks can be hired too if you would rather sit.
dir.tip: Go early: Zurich's transport authority notes that the mood on the lake is at its best in the morning. Note that the Strandbad's own entry fee is not part of the rental.
dir.near: ZVV stop Mythenquai

prices: Bath entry (not included) – adults / from 16 / from 6
dir.offers: One of three Supkultur city stations (Tiefenbrunnen, Mythenquai, Utoquai). Board rental by the hour, courses and lessons.
dir.ohNote: 09:00-20:00 depending on weather; the bath may close early in bad weather (page states both 'from 14:00' and 'from 11:00'). Call ahead in changeable weather.
dir.req: Swimming ability required. Teens from 14 may rent a board on their own; children under 30 kg can ride on an adult's SUP. Rental includes board, one paddle per person, life vest and dry bag. Bath entry fee not included. Reservations only for groups of 5+.
dir.about: Over on the eastern shore, at Strandbad Tiefenbrunnen on Bellerivestrasse, this is Supkultur's second walk-up station, a handy choice if you live in Seefeld or Riesbach. The setup mirrors Mythenquai: boards by the hour, kayaks for anyone who prefers to sit, and courses or private lessons that can be booked in advance. From here you launch onto the wider stretch of water towards Zollikon, with views of the city and, on clear days, the Alps. It works well for beginners who want a staffed base, and for confident paddlers heading off on a longer loop along the Gold Coast side.
dir.tip: In changeable weather the bath can close early and the station may not be staffed, so ring ahead before you set off. Groups of five or more can reserve; everyone else is first come, first served.
dir.near: ZVV stop Wildbachstrasse

prices: Bath entry (not included) – adults / from 16 / from 6
dir.notes: The Utoquai station is for holders of a Supkultur SUP subscription (SUP-Abo); day rental is at Mythenquai and Tiefenbrunnen.
dir.offers: Subscription station of Supkultur.
dir.ohNote: Seebad hours. Subscription-only station, no hourly rental; staffed only when needed - sales and introductions by appointment (book 24 h ahead). Open in all weather.
dir.req: Subscription holders only. Swimming ability required. Mandatory in-person introduction (~20 min incl. paperwork) before first use. Subscriptions are personal and non-transferable.
dir.about: At the historic Seebad Utoquai, close to Bellevue and the opera house, Supkultur keeps a station reserved for subscription holders rather than casual renters. If you paddle several times a week, this is the most central launch on the lake: you step off the wooden bath straight into the lower basin, with the Grossmünster towers and the quays of the old town close by. There is no hourly hire here, so first-timers should head to Mythenquai or Tiefenbrunnen instead. Regulars like it for after-work sessions and early mornings, when the water in front of the city is at its calmest and you can be back at your desk soon after.
dir.tip: Before your first session you need a short in-person introduction (about 20 minutes including paperwork); book it at least 24 hours ahead.
dir.near: ZVV stop Utoquai

dir.n: SUPSWISS – Stand Up Paddle school & rental
dir.hours: Board rental: Fri–Sat 12:00–20:00, Sun 12:00–18:00 · Shop (Steinstrasse 75, 8003 Zürich): Wed–Fri 11:00–19:00, Sat 09:00–16:00
dir.offers: Courses at different levels, SUP adventure tours on Lake Zurich and across Switzerland, board rental (bookable separately), events.
dir.status: Unconfirmed: the SUPSWISS website now redirects to kiteswiss.ch — call before you go.
dir.about: Down in Wollishofen, next to the Rote Fabrik and the Ziegel oh Lac restaurant, SUPSWISS teaches stand-up paddling from the community centre on Bachstrasse. It calls itself a certified SUP school, and the focus is on courses at several levels rather than pure walk-up hire, although boards can be rented separately. Beyond the home bay it has run adventure tours on other Swiss lakes, plus themed sessions such as sunset yoga and paddling with your dog. The southern end of the city shore is less busy than the central quays, which makes it a calm place to learn. Check the current offer before you go: the old web address now forwards to kiteswiss.ch.
dir.tip: Reach it by tram 7 or S-Bahn to Wollishofen, or arrive by lake boat.
dir.near: Tram 7 / S8, S24 to Wollishofen · ZVV stop Post Wollishofen

dir.offers: Vintage 1970s pedalos (first come, first served), rowing boats, boats with (electric) motor that can partly be reserved, and a sauna boat for up to 6 people.
dir.oh: Mar,Apr,Oct Mo-Fr 13:00-18:00; Mar,Apr,Oct Sa,Su 11:30-18:30; May,Sep Mo-Fr 13:00-19:00; May,Sep Sa,Su 11:00-19:00; Jun-Aug Mo-Fr 13:00-20:00; Jun-Aug Sa,Su 10:00-20:00
dir.ohNote: Hours may change due to weather; no launches during a storm warning (free rebooking or cancellation). Part of the fleet is kept for walk-ins; sauna boats booked online independently of these hours. Contact page does not label the hours with a year.
dir.req: Cash deposit and an official ID (ID card or passport) at check-in. Pedalos from age 12 without parental supervision; licence-free motorboats from 18; licence boats, Shortbreak 5.8 e-boats and Otter e-pedalos from 22. Licence boats need a licence valid for inland waters (international certificate only with a valid national licence). Life jackets on board (emergency use; children should bring their own). Billed per quarter hour at the hourly rate after return.
dir.about: Right beside the Seebad Enge and its Badi bar on Mythenquai, this hire stand has one of the most central jetties on the lake. The fleet is a mix of 1970s pedal boats, rowing boats for anyone who wants a workout, and motorboats with petrol or electric engines that need no licence. The unusual extra is a sauna boat for up to six people, with the lake as your plunge pool. Out on the lower basin you get a wide view back over the city. Families, couples and groups of friends all fit, and the site is listed as accessible for prams and many wheelchair users.
dir.tip: Pedalos cannot be reserved, so arrive early on summer weekends; some motorboats can be booked online in advance. Bring cash for the deposit and an ID card or passport.
dir.near: ZVV stop Rentenanstalt

dir.offers: Pedal boats, rowing boats and motorboats; wakeboard equipment for hire.
dir.ohNote: CLOSED: the official site states 'Die Bootsvermietung ist geschlossen' - operators Rytz+Kreuzer retired after 20 years; a new team plans to open a new rental in 2027.
dir.closed: Closed: the operators retired after 20 years; a new team plans a new rental for 2027 (operator website, checked 10 Oct 2026).

dir.season: Daily in summer; reduced timetable in spring, autumn and winter
prices: Mini lake cruise (1 h), 2nd class – adults / children
Short lake cruise (1.5 h), 2nd class – adults / children
Long lake cruise (4.5 h), 2nd class – adults / children
Long lake cruise (4.5 h), 1st class – adults / children

dir.offers: Mini lake cruise to Wollishofen (60 min), short cruise to Thalwil/Erlenbach (90 min), grand cruise Zürich–Rapperswil and back (4½ h). Mini and short cruises are free with the Zürich Card.
dir.ohNote: Scheduled cruises; 2026 timetable valid 14.12.2025-12.12.2026 (departures in the PDF timetable). Prices are one-way tickets.
dir.about: From the piers at Bürkliplatz, at the lake end of Bahnhofstrasse, the Zürichsee-Schifffahrtsgesellschaft runs the lake's scheduled boats, including paddle steamers such as the Stadt Zürich. Three round trips are pitched at visitors: a one-hour mini cruise down to Wollishofen, a 90-minute loop to Thalwil and Erlenbach, and a long day out to Rapperswil and back. You see the city and both shores from the water rather than the road. Themed evening boats add fondue, brunch, barbecue or dance nights. The shorter cruises make an easy first look at the lake for visitors and families alike.
dir.tip: The mini and short cruises are free with the Zürich Card. In dry spells low water can restrict sailings, so check the ZSG timetable page on the day.
dir.near: ZVV stop Bürkliplatz

dir.offers: Outdoor standing wave next to Hardbrücke station. 30-minute slots for up to six surfers, bookable online or on site, with instruction and supervision; free entry for spectators, bar and food.
dir.ohNote: Hours as currently published on the operator's contact page; hours can change - call +41 76 224 42 24 if unsure. Free entry for spectators.
dir.req: Bring an ID card or vehicle registration document. Kids: no fear of water, good swimmers, at least 30 kg, helmet and an adult present; minimum age at parents' discretion. Fitting wetsuit provided on site; own boards (up to 6'2", leash required) and wetsuits allowed. Liability waiver (can be completed at home).
dir.about: Tucked between the railway tracks and Frau Gerolds Garten in Zurich West, a few steps from Hardbrücke station, Urbansurf is an outdoor standing wave close to the Prime Tower. Up to six surfers share each 30-minute slot, taking turns on an endless wave framed by padded walls and deep enough water to make falls forgiving. Instructors supervise and help novices find their feet, while experienced riders can bring their own short board. Around the pool there is a bar, food and regular live music, and spectators get in free, so it works as an evening out even for friends who stay dry. Few places let you surf in the middle of a city.
dir.tip: Bring an ID card or vehicle registration document to check in. Children need to be good swimmers, weigh at least 30 kg and wear a helmet, with an adult present.
dir.near: Zürich Hardbrücke station · a few minutes' walk

dir.n: TSK Zürich – PADI 5 Star dive centre
prices: PADI Open Water Diver – registration fee
CHF 60.00 per participant (course price not shown on the page)
PADI Discover Scuba Diving (2 h, pool)
dir.offers: PADI scuba diving, freediving and snorkelling courses from beginner to professional, first aid (EFR), adaptive diving.
dir.req: Open Water Diver: minimum age 15 (10 for Junior OWD), good swimming skills, medical certificate not older than 1 year; own ABC gear (mask, snorkel, footies, fins). Discover Scuba Diving: minimum age 10 (8 for Bubblemaker), good swimming skills; full equipment included.
dir.about: Stauffacherquai, on the Sihl in Kreis 4, is home to TSK Zürich, which describes itself as the largest dive school and shop in the region. It is a PADI 5 Star IDC centre with around 45 instructors, teaching everything from first try-dives and snorkelling to freediving, first aid and instructor-level courses, in German or English. Adaptive diving for people with disabilities is part of the programme. Lake Zurich is the home water, and the club side runs weekend trips, Sunday dive outings and events for non-divers too. The shop sells, rents and services gear, fills tanks, and has its own bar with beer on tap, which says something about the social atmosphere.
dir.tip: For the Open Water course bring your own mask, snorkel, boots and fins plus a medical certificate under a year old; the rest of the kit is provided.
dir.near: Parking on site (PADI listing)

prices: Open Water Diver – Gold (incl. Nitrox, flexible dates)
Open Water Diver – Platin (private, incl. Nitrox)
Open Water Diver – Diamant (private, incl. Nitrox + Mares kit on loan)
dir.offers: Try dives, nitrox, technical and rebreather training, underwater photography, courses for children and for people with disabilities, pool training.
dir.ohNote: Shop hours. Sunday and outside these hours by appointment. Emergency number 079 473 58 53.
dir.req: Open Water Diver: minimum age 10, must be able to swim, good health; online theory must be completed before the course. Rental equipment included except ABC (mask, snorkel, fins).
dir.about: In Seefeld, on Zollikerstrasse a few streets back from the lake, Poseidon combines a dive school, shop and workshop. Courses start with try-dives and run through nitrox, technical diving and rebreather training, with underwater photography, children's courses and teaching for divers with disabilities alongside. Pool sessions cover the basics before you head to the lake. The workshop handles regulator servicing and neoprene repairs, and the team fills nitrox and trimix, so technical divers come here for gas as much as for lessons. Reviews praise the instructors and the advice in the shop, and the school also leads trips to river sites in Ticino such as the Verzasca.
dir.tip: Poseidon is the nearest listed fill station for the Tiefenbrunnen (WZT) shore dive, so it is a practical stop before a lake dive on the east shore.

dir.addr: c/o Zürcher Yacht Club, General-Guisan-Quai 17, 8002 Zürich
dir.offers: Sailing for children: beginner course without experience (sails, tiller, manoeuvres, knots) and an advanced course; school holidays or Wednesdays/Fridays during term.
dir.about: Children learn to sail in Optimist dinghies here, operating as a guest of the Zürcher Yacht Club on General-Guisan-Quai, right by Bürkliplatz and the Arboretum. No experience is needed for the beginner course: young sailors rig the sail, steer with the tiller, practise simple manoeuvres, learn a little theory and tie their first sailor's knots. Those who want more move on to an advanced course that teaches handling the boat in stronger wind, the path to becoming an Opti skipper. Lessons run as holiday courses or on Wednesdays or Fridays during term, so it fits around school. The setting, in the lower basin in front of the city, is about as central as sailing gets.
dir.tip: Come by tram 7, 11 or 13 to Bürkliplatz. If you drive, park at Hafen Enge and walk about five minutes to the yacht club.
dir.near: Tram 7, 11, 13 to Bürkliplatz · car: Hafen Enge, about 5 min walk

dir.offers: Sailing (listed under sailing schools).
Sailing and motorboat school.
dir.about: Based on the Rote Fabrik site in Wollishofen, SMS Zürisee has its own jetty on the city's southern shore and teaches both sailing and motorboat driving, from first lessons up to the offshore licence. Alongside licence training it offers wakeboarding and wakesurfing behind its boats, and boats can also be rented. The mix of licence school and towed sports makes it unusual: you might come for your boat licence and come back for a wake session. Booking runs through its online portal, with lessons and rentals scheduled individually.
dir.tip: The meeting point is given as Seestrasse 395, at the Rote Fabrik. Cancel at least 48 hours ahead for driving lessons and rentals, 24 hours for watersports.

dir.offers: Motorboat driving school (Swiss boat licence).
dir.about: Beni Winiger is a federally recognised motorboat and sailing instructor who prepares learners for the Swiss boat licence, categories A and D, and says he has taken more than 3,500 candidates to the exam. The meeting point in Zurich is the Restaurant Seerose in Wollishofen, with a second base in Horgen on the left shore. Lessons are held only inside the official exam area, so every hour on the water rehearses the real test, and the boats have cabins and heating, which matters on a cold spring evening. Teaching is in German or English. It suits anyone who wants a straightforward, exam-focused route to driving a boat on Lake Zurich.
dir.tip: The listing notes the lessons take place only in the exam area and the boats are heated, so early- and late-season lessons are realistic. Ask which meeting point applies (Wollishofen, Tiefenbrunnen, Horgen, Thalwil or Herrliberg are named).
dir.near: Meeting point Restaurant Seerose, Wollishofen · parking available (local.ch)

dir.addr: Seestrasse 31, 8712 Stäfa · also Uetikon am See
dir.offers: Sailing and motorboat school.
dir.about: With more than 40 years of teaching behind it, Beat Lang's school trains sailors and motorboat drivers on the right shore of the lake, with courses held mainly in Uetikon am See and Stäfa. The modular system lets you book up to 16 weekly appointments, so you can fit lessons around work rather than taking a block week. Beyond the licence itself there is further training and preparation for offshore sailing. Lessons last between one and a half and two and a half hours depending on group size. Learning away from the city end of the lake means fewer crowds on the water.
dir.tip: Students, apprentices and pupils get a 15 percent discount; book online or by phone.

dir.n: Ceccotorenas – wakeboard school, SUP & pedalos Stäfa
dir.hours: Wakeboard, wakesurf, wakefoil: daily 09:00–21:00 by phone reservation · Office: daily 10:00–18:00 · SUP and pedalos daily in good weather
prices: Wakeboard / wakeskate, 15-min session incl. gear, driver, coaching – adults
SUP rental incl. paddle and leash – 1 hour
dir.offers: Wakeboard, wakesurf and wakefoil sessions with coaching; SUP rental (reserve by phone); 9 pedalos, some with a slide (no reservation; sunset and moonlight trips bookable); small shop; events. Runs the Stäfa pedalo rental for the Verkehrsverein Stäfa.
dir.about: At Stäfa harbour on the right shore, next to the village pedalo rental it also runs, Ceccotorenas is a wakeboard school with a boat and a driver for hire by the hour. Riders of all ages come for wakeboard, wakeskate and wakesurf coaching, and more experienced riders can try wakefoiling, which lifts you above the water even at low speed once you have the technique. Kit for all four disciplines can be hired. If towed sports are not your thing, there are SUP boards and pedalos, some with a slide, for a slower afternoon. It is one of the few places on the lake where a mixed group can split between action and lazing about.
dir.tip: Opening times depend on season and weather, so check the website before travelling; Stäfa station is the nearest stop.
dir.near: Stäfa railway station (ZVV stop Stäfa, Bahnhof)

dir.addr: Office: Bruneggstrasse 1, 8634 Hombrechtikon · courses in Stäfa, Feldbach and on the Greifensee
prices: Adult keelboat basic course, private (8 × 2 h)
dir.offers: Children’s sailing school in Stäfa (Optimist and Laser, 5 × 2½ h, four levels); adult keelboat lessons in Feldbach, Stäfa and Greifensee, including the Swiss D licence, spinnaker training and refreshers.
dir.notes: Pin shows the Stäfa course area; the office is in Hombrechtikon.
dir.req: Life jacket must be worn at all times on board (adult lessons). Accident insurance is the participant's/parents' responsibility. Lessons cancellable free up to 72 h ahead; subscriptions paid in advance, non-refundable.
dir.about: Thomas Zwick runs a small sailing school split across two age groups. Children and teenagers sail Optimists and Lasers at Kehlhof in Stäfa, in courses of five sessions spread over four levels, so a child can progress from first outing to confident dinghy sailor. Adults learn on keelboats from Feldbach and Stäfa on Lake Zurich, or near the town of Greifensee, mostly as private lessons. The adult side covers the Swiss D licence, spinnaker handling and refresher sessions for anyone who has not sailed in years. A reviewer describes a small club feel with a motivated team, which suits nervous beginners better than a large school.
dir.tip: Life jackets are worn at all times on adult lessons, and lessons can be cancelled free of charge up to 72 hours ahead.

dir.offers: Pedalos with or without slide, electric boats (E-Tuckerli), lounge boat and motorboat – all without licence; trips e.g. to the island of Lützelau.
dir.ohNote: Boat rental Rapperswil closed from 01.10.2026 (season end).
dir.req: ID must be deposited in advance. Life jackets mandatory outside the shore zone (300 m).
dir.about: Down at Rapperswil harbour, below the old town and castle, Hensa hires out pedalos, a small electric boat called the E-Tuckerli, a lounge boat and motorboats, none of which need a licence. The obvious outing is across to Lützelau, the little wooded island off the shore, which takes a steady pedal and gives you somewhere to aim for. You can just as well drift in the bay with the Seedamm and the Upper Lake behind you. Families like the pedalos, and couples or friends tend to take the lounge boat. The harbour is a short walk from Rapperswil station, so it is easy to combine with a day in the town.
dir.tip: Life jackets are mandatory once you leave the 300 m shore zone, and you leave an ID as deposit. The rental season ends on 30 September.
dir.near: Rapperswil station

dir.n: Kuster Sport – canoe & SUP station Schmerikon
dir.addr: Station: Hafen Schmerikon · Shop: St. Gallerstrasse 72, 8716 Schmerikon
dir.hours: Kayak & SUP station at the harbour: daily, April to end of September (book online). Shop: Tu–Fr 09:00–12:00 and 13:30–18:30, Sa 09:00–16:00.
dir.offers: Rental of kayaks, canoes, rafting boats and SUP boards, bookable via website or app.
dir.ohNote: These are shop hours (St. Gallerstrasse 72). The kayak & SUP station at the harbour is open daily April to end of September and bookable online around the clock.
dir.about: Schmerikon harbour, at the far eastern tip of the Upper Lake, is where Kuster Sport keeps a self-service canoe and SUP station at Schmerikon harbour, while its shop on St. Gallerstrasse handles winter sports in the cold months. Kayaks, Canadian canoes, rafts and paddleboards can all be booked online or through the app at any hour. From here you can paddle out onto the Obersee, with the Linth plain and the Glarus mountains behind, or follow the Linth itself, which makes this a good starting point for a river-and-lake day. It suits people who want their own boat for a few hours without owning one, from couples to small groups in a raft.
dir.tip: The harbour station runs daily from April to the end of September even when the shop is closed; the nearest stop is Schmerikon, Brücke.
dir.near: ZVV stop Schmerikon, Brücke

dir.addr: Contact: Gütschstrasse 20, 8122 Binz · boats at Maur on the Greifensee
dir.offers: Boats for hire by the hour on the Greifensee; contact the association to rent.
dir.about: Run by volunteers, the Verschönerungsverein (village improvement society) of Maur maintains a few boats on the eastern shore of the Greifensee and hires them out by the hour. It is a low-key, volunteer arrangement rather than a commercial hire stand: you contact the association to book. Motorboats are banned on the Greifensee apart from the passenger ferry, so the water stays quiet, with the Pfannenstiel hills rising behind the village. It suits anyone after a calm hour on the water rather than a busy harbour scene.
dir.tip: Since 1 April 2025 the canton of Zurich has had a boat registration and cleaning rule, so ask the association what applies when you book.

dir.n: Kayakfun – kayak & mini-raft rental with shuttle
dir.offers: Self-guided trips on the Reuss, Limmat, Aare and Hallwilersee with instruction and life jacket; shuttle drops boats at your put-in and collects you at the end.
dir.ohNote: Rental April to October; holidays/closures listed on the Kayakfun website. Instruction and life jacket provided.
dir.about: Based in Mellingen, a few minutes from Heitersberg/Mellingen station, Kayakfun rents boats for self-guided trips on the Aargau rivers, the Reuss, Limmat and Aare, and on the Hallwilersee. The point of difference is the shuttle: the team drives your boat in a van to the put-in, sets it up and collects you at the end, so you never have to paddle back upstream. Choose a stable sit-on-top kayak, recommended for first-timers, or a Grabner mini-raft if you want more room for two. Each trip starts with instruction and a life jacket. It suits beginners and relaxed groups who want a river day without arranging transport.
dir.tip: Take the train to Heitersberg/Mellingen; the base is about five minutes on foot from the station.
dir.near: Heitersberg/Mellingen station · 5 min walk

prices: VIP member with equipment rental – month
VIP member with equipment rental – season
dir.offers: Kitesurf and wingfoil school for all levels, kite shop, rental and test gear (kites, wings, boards, foils, wetsuits, SUP), SUP self-service station; kitebeach access needs a membership.
dir.req: Kitebeach: club membership mandatory (bought on site); liability insurance covering kitesurfing in Switzerland; licensed kitesurfer VDWS level 4 or IKO level 3J; good swimmer; one authorised entry point to the lake.
dir.about: Swiss Kitesurf runs its school and shop right beside the kitebeach at the Mulets sports centre in Silvaplana, at about 1,800 m in the Upper Engadine. Group, semi-private, private and foil lessons cover kitesurfing and wingfoiling, and the shop rents and tests kites, wings, boards and foils, with a repair service for when things go wrong. Everything sits within about 200 metres: the beach, changing rooms and showers in the sports centre, a kite bar and Restaurant Mulets with its sun terrace, plus a campsite on the lake. Beginners learn on the same water where experienced riders chase the afternoon Maloja wind, with the peaks of the Engadine all around.
dir.tip: The thermal south-westerly usually fills in from about 1 pm and blows until sunset, so book morning lessons for theory and the afternoon for time on the water.

dir.offers: Switzerland’s best-known kite lake: thermal Maloja wind from early afternoon, blowing about 80% of days June–September, often 20–25 knots between 15:00 and 17:00.
dir.notes: Kitebeach access requires a membership with the local kite school.
dir.req: Kitebeach: club membership mandatory (bought on site); liability insurance covering kitesurfing in Switzerland; licensed kitesurfer VDWS level 4 or IKO level 3J; good swimmer; one authorised entry point to the lake.
dir.about: High in the Upper Engadine, Lake Silvaplana is Switzerland's best-known kite lake because of the Maloja wind, a thermal south-westerly that typically sets in around 1 pm and blows until sunset at 4 to 5 Beaufort, stronger with a south-westerly airflow. North winds are less reliable. The launch is a leased private meadow at the Mulets sports centre, with marshals on duty in season, and there is a single authorised entry point to the lake. It is a spot for independent riders; newcomers should start with the school on the beach.
dir.tip: Kitebeach access needs a season or day membership bought on site, liability insurance that covers kiting in Switzerland, and proof of level (VDWS 4 or IKO 3J).

dir.offers: Lake spot with pebble beach; small chop.
dir.notes: Since 2021 starting from Isleten is allowed only for club members and day members. Independent kitesurfing only.
dir.about: Isleten sits on the western shore of the Urnersee, the southern arm of Lake Lucerne, where steep limestone walls drop into the water. The beach is pebbly and the chop small. Unlike Silvaplana, this is not a thermal spot: the windiest months are December to March, when Föhn storms funnel down the Reuss valley, and summer days with wind are rare. Spot statistics count about 61 days a year with at least 12 knots. On big Föhn days the lake has seen gusts well above 40 knots, so it is strictly for independent, experienced riders who can judge gusty mountain wind.
dir.tip: Since 2021 launching at Isleten has been allowed only for club members and day members, so sort out membership before you rig.

dir.offers: IKO kite school operating since 2016 from the port of Flüelen.
dir.status: Unconfirmed: a 2024 canton of Uri list still names this school (Beckenried), but a kite directory says it is likely closed — call before you go.
dir.about: Operating on the Urnersee since 2016, this IKO kite school has worked from the port of Flüelen at the southern end of the lake, running sessions from a large boat rather than from the beach. Its spot is the Föhn-driven Urnersee around Isleten, where launching from shore is restricted to club members. Independent kiting skills are required for its boat sessions. Its current status is unclear: a kite directory now marks the school as likely closed, while the canton of Uri still listed it at an address in Beckenried in late 2024. Contact the school directly before planning a trip.
dir.tip: Confirm by phone or e-mail that the school is operating before you travel, as listings disagree.

dir.addr: Reuss, Bremgarten AG (near the military grounds)
dir.offers: Standing river wave, surfable at water levels of about 1.8–2.6 m, mostly May to September.
dir.notes: Experienced surfers only; river conditions change quickly.
dir.about: At Bremgarten in Aargau, near the military grounds, the Reuss forms a standing wave where fast water runs over a sill into slower water. It is one of the best-known river waves in Switzerland and part of what has made the town a centre of the Swiss surf scene. The wave works when the river level is roughly between 1.8 and 2.6 metres, mostly from May to September. Because the Reuss flows relatively slowly here, locals recommend a short board with a wide tail. There is no operator, no lifeguard and no fee: you surf at your own risk in a river whose conditions change quickly.
dir.tip: Check the river gauge before you drive; outside the 1.8–2.6 m window the wave is not surfable.

dir.offers: River wave at the wooden sluice bridge where the Aare leaves Lake Thun; glacial water, mostly surfed in spring.
dir.req: Experienced river surfers only. Surfed without rope (rope only on the rear wave, on the provided hook) and generally without leash. Usual kit: board, wetsuit, possibly booties, helmet, buoyancy/impact vest. No membership required. Rear wave works only with enough discharge, mainly in spring; gate positions change several times a day (gauge: hydrodaten.admin.ch station 2030).
dir.about: In the middle of Thun, the Aare surges through the wooden sluice gates of the Mühleschleuse just after leaving Lake Thun, and spectators watch from the bridge above Mühleplatz. The wave is glacial, shallow and fast, with large stones under the surface and the main current running straight at a bridge pillar, so a fall gives you only seconds to get clear. The rear wave can be surfed holding a rope; the one nearest the bridge, nicknamed the Monster, mostly works in spring and has snapped boards and fins. Gate positions change several times a day. This is for experienced river surfers only; beginners are pointed to the deeper Scherzligschleuse wave instead.
dir.tip: Gate settings and flow change during the day, so check the federal gauge (hydrodaten.admin.ch station 2030) and watch a few rides before paddling in.

dir.offers: Bungee surfing from a 3 m bridge on the Reuss, mostly in summer.
dir.about: Bungee surfing on the Reuss in Lucerne happens mainly at the Geissmattbrücke, a bridge about 3 metres above the river downstream of the old town. A rider is held by an elastic line anchored on the bridge, which builds tension and slings them onto the current so they can ride the flowing water like a wave. Other bridges as far as Emmen are used too, but this stretch sees most of the action, mostly in summer. The water is cold and the river fast, so this is not for casual swimmers. There is no operator or supervision; talk to local riders before you try it.
dir.tip: Get to know the local scene first: experienced riders can explain where the line is anchored and how the current behaves at the bridge.

dir.n: OANA Citywave – indoor wave, Mall of Switzerland
prices: Basic Session (45 min, beginners, intro & coaching)
Hardtop board rental in Advanced session
dir.offers: Indoor standing wave adjustable for all levels, warm water.
dir.ohNote: Wave, desk & shop hours. Reduced hours on some holidays (e.g. 24.12.2026 10-16). Café & bar have separate hours.
dir.req: Minimum age 8 and height 1 m; under 16 only with written parental consent and helmet. Liability waiver for all surfers. Check in 20 min before. Bring swimwear and towel; softtop board included, wetsuit available on site.
dir.about: Inside the Mall of Switzerland in Ebikon, just outside Lucerne, OANA runs what it calls Switzerland's only indoor surf spot, a Citywave standing wave in a 1,200 m² hall with warm water. The wave can be tuned from gentle for first-timers to steep and powerful for advanced manoeuvres, so mixed groups can surf the same session at different settings. Because it is indoors, it runs all year regardless of weather. The Bowlery restaurant looks straight onto the wave, which makes it easy for family and friends to watch, and the venue hosts birthdays and company events. A softtop board comes with each session and wetsuits are available.
dir.tip: From Lucerne the S1 to Buchrain takes under ten minutes, then it is a two-minute walk. Surfers under 16 need written parental consent and a helmet.
dir.near: S1 to Buchrain · 2 min walk · buses 1, 23, 111 stop by the entrance · Mall of Switzerland car park (paid)

prices: Coached session (1 h surf, beginner-intermediate, all equipment included)
dir.offers: Wavegarden wave pool producing 300–1,000 waves per hour, water 16–25 °C.
dir.ohNote: 2026 season opened 3-4 April 2026. Opening times vary by season (reception opens 1 h before the first session and closes 1 h after the last) - check the session schedule.
dir.req: Coached: beginner to intermediate, all equipment included. Guided: must be autonomous in the ocean. Free Surf: must be validated for free surf. Packs include softboard, wetsuit & winter kit.
dir.about: Sion's Domaine des Iles, in the Rhône valley between vineyards and snow-capped peaks, is home to Alaïa Bay, a Wavegarden Cove pool that produces between 300 and 1,000 waves an hour. Each session is set to one level, from gentle Waikiki rollers for beginners through Malibu, Advanced and Expert to Pro and the punishing Beast Mode, so nobody shares the water with surfers far above or below them. Coached sessions include board and wetsuit, and there is surfing after dark under lights. The Twin Fin restaurant terrace overlooks the pool. At the time of writing it was described as the only commercial Cove-technology pool in continental Europe.
dir.tip: The Twin Fin restaurant does not take reservations, so arrive early for a terrace seat; experts should limit themselves to a couple of sessions a day.
dir.near: Bus 361 or B12 from Sion station to Sion, Tennis îles (stop in front) · large car park by Tennis des Iles

dir.offers: Lake dive site described by divers as suitable for beginners and night dives.
dir.notes: Depth, entry and local rules are not verified — ask a dive centre.
dir.about: Tiefenbrunnen's water sports centre, on Zurich's eastern shore, has a wide staircase with a handrail, or a jetty, to take you into the lake. The bottom drops to about 3 m beyond the edge, then slopes gently down to around 25 m, with the listed maximum at 30 m. Divers have placed a series of objects along the slope, including pipes, sunken boats, a diving bell, statues and signs, which give you something to navigate by. The gentle gradient makes it a popular training and buoyancy site, and reviewers recommend it for night dives. Poseidon on Zollikerstrasse is the nearest listed fill station.
dir.tip: Parking is close to the entry; Poseidon in Seefeld is the nearest listed air fill.
dir.near: Parking near the entry

dir.offers: Lake dive site used for training with instructors.
dir.notes: Depth, entry and local rules are not verified — ask a dive centre.
dir.about: Herrliberg's large car park on Seestrasse, on the right shore, is only steps from an easy entry. The site is marked with buoys chained to the bottom, and a stepped rock wall runs from about 5 m down to 30 m, with seagrass meadows and plenty of fish in the shallows. Many divers do their first open-water dives here with an instructor, so it is busy with training groups. There can be some current, and in summer you share the shore with swimmers, a snack stand and public toilets. Shops in Horgen, Wädenswil and Zurich are the nearest for fills.
dir.tip: Parking is free at the large car park; watch out for swimmers at the entry in summer.
dir.near: Free parking at the large car park on Seestrasse

dir.offers: Lake dive site on the Au peninsula.
dir.notes: Depth, entry and local rules are not verified — ask a dive centre.
dir.about: Deep wall diving is the draw at the Au peninsula near Wädenswil, and it is for advanced divers only. You enter left of the passenger-boat pier, descend to about 10 m where the wall begins, and follow it on your left shoulder towards 35–40 m. After five to seven minutes you reach a single standing stone, about 10 m off the wall, then a tree lying across the gap at around 40 m, and beyond it a fissured wall where burbot hide. On the way back small caves sit at 18–20 m and at 11 m. Two arm-thick intake pipes near the pier pillars mark the exit. The listed maximum depth is about 52 m.
dir.tip: Passenger boats dock at the pier, with the first summer arrival at 10:32, so dive early and be out of the water before then.
dir.near: Park at Landgasthof Au, then about 300 m downhill to the boat pier (steep walk back)

dir.offers: Lake dive site at the Horn in Richterswil.
dir.notes: Depth, entry and local rules are not verified — ask a dive centre.
dir.about: A little meadow with a bench at the Horn, the small headland in Richterswil beside the youth hostel, leads to a stone staircase into the water. The bottom starts as stone, turns to silt and opens into a seagrass meadow, with a maximum depth of about 10 m, which makes it a beginner-level shore dive. A training platform sits at about 5 m. Two dive schools are based in Richterswil, so you will often meet course groups. It is a relaxed, shallow site for a first lake dive or for checking new kit rather than one for deep exploration.
dir.tip: The platform at 5 m is private property of the Local Diving school; register by phone before using it.
dir.near: Parking garage near the youth hostel / Seeclub Richterswil

dir.offers: Lake dive site at Rüschlikon.
dir.notes: Depth, entry and local rules are not verified — ask a dive centre.
dir.about: The Pumphüsli site in Rüschlikon, on the left shore, has parking right next to the entry, toilets and a covered spot to change when it rains. A wide staircase with a railing takes you over a bottom of small stones straight out to about 5 m, where a bicycle saddle on a long pole marks a good place for the safety stop. Turning right brings you to a sunken boat at about 10 m. On the way back, dense weed beds at 5 m hold shoals of small fish and the occasional pike, with sunlight playing through the green water. It suits beginners and divers returning after a break.
dir.tip: Use the bicycle saddle on its pole at about 5 m as your marker for the three-minute safety stop.
dir.near: Parking right next to the site

dir.offers: Dive site at Maur harbour on the Greifensee.
dir.notes: Depth, entry and local rules are not verified — ask a dive centre.
dir.about: Beside the harbour in Maur on the Greifensee, divers enter about 50 m left of the boat landing using the rowing-boat ramp and jetty. You must swim only to the left: the harbour basin to the right is off limits. The muddy bottom slopes very gently to about 12 m, with roots, tree trunks and a few perch, and visibility is usually just 1–2 m, so good buoyancy matters. About 20 minutes out you reach a yacht mooring with chains and buoy lines, and fishing lines are common near the entry. Motorboats are banned on the lake apart from the ferry, and diving is allowed only at certain spots.
dir.tip: Diving on the Greifensee is restricted to designated places; check the current rules with a local dive centre before you go.
dir.near: Parking by the lake opposite the church; tight in midsummer

rules.t: City of Zürich: windsurfing and kitesurfing are not allowed north of the line Wollishofen landing stage – Tiefenbrunnen harbour (south mole), within 150 m of ship landing stages, near public baths and harbour entrances. The first 150 m from the shore are mainly for bathers. Daylight and clear visibility only.
Canton of Zürich: since 1 March 2015 there are zones on Lake Zurich where kitesurfing is prohibited (map on the source page). Check the zones before you launch.

Canton of Schwyz: kitesurfing is banned on all navigable waters except Lake Zug and the Wägitalersee; the 150 m shore zone may only be crossed to launch and land. Further restrictions apply on the Schwyz parts of Lake Zurich (Frauenwinkel, Hurden, eastern Obersee).
